text:
maria: FYI escalation from AcmePayments (Zendesk). They report intermittent 5xx/504s on hosted inference endpoints for ~2h, high error rate on /v1/generate and streaming. Customer gave two request IDs: req-abc123 and req-def456. They say SDK retries just loop and latency spikes to 30s before failing. Pasting their minimal repro and error snippet below.

Customer paste:
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: req-abc123

{ "model": "redwood-2.1", "input": "summarize: ...", "stream": false }

Response: 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":"gateway timeout","trace":"trace-xyz","request_id":"req-abc123"}
```

maria: I opened ticket #Z-1842 and attached their request/response and tokenized logs. Can someone check any correlated infra alerts in prod-west-1? @sre-bot any signals? :eyes:

sre-bot: ALERT: [prod-west-1] gateway-5xx-rate spike detected at 2026-03-15T09:10:00Z. 5xx rate = 18% over 5m (baseline 0.8%). Top upstream code: 502/504. Linked alert: https://monitoring.example/alert/8472

josh: copying. Thanks @maria. Can you pull the exact request ids + timestamps? I'll tail the gateway and runtime traces. Also we should check autoscaler decisions and queue depth for the dedicated pools that host this tenant.

samir: likely causes: autoscaler thrash, model eviction/weight-load storms, or a bad kernel on that instance. Do we have kernel eviction logs? Also ask customer whether they changed concurrency or are sending large batch requests.

maria: sent timestamps to you in DM. I did a quick repro from my laptop against the same endpoint with the customer's header. Repro below.

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPRO_KEY" -H "X-Request-ID: repro-1785" -d '{"model":"redwood-2.1","input":"hello","stream":false}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
* Connected to api.redwood.example (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Authorization: Bearer ********
> X-Request-ID: repro-1785
> Content-Type: application/json
> Content-Length: 48

< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
< Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:21:13 GMT
< Content-Type: application/json
< Content-Length: 78

{"error":"upstream error","upstream_status":502,"request_id":"repro-1785","hint":"upstream: runtime process returned 502"}
```

maria: Also pulled gateway logs for repro-1785: shows L7 gateway returned 502 because upstream connection reset: `upstream reset: connection closed while sending body`. Runtime log snippet from candidate pod:```
[2026-03-15T09:21:12Z] error: worker 8421 failed to handle request repro-1785: kernel-fallback exception during kv-cache restore
[2026-03-15T09:21:12Z] warn: evicting model redwood-2.1@sha:abcd due to memory pressure
[2026-03-15T09:21:12Z] info: starting model load redwood-2.1@sha:ef01 on instance i-0a12
```

josh: that model eviction stamp lines up w/ scales. I'm seeing a surge of model loads and OOMs in the infra graphs. tail of kube events shows repeated pod restarts for the runtime deployment (runtime-prod-west-1) around 09:18-09:24. Pasting kubectl events snippet:```
Events:
  09:18:55 Pod runtime-8421 BackOff restarting failed container
  09:19:03 Pod runtime-8421 OOMKilled
  09:20:11 Pod runtime-8421 Started container runtime
  09:22:30 Pod runtime-8422 CrashLoopBackOff
```

josh: short-term mitigation: route the customer to a stable model variant (less memory) and increase gateway backend timeout to 90s for their requests while we stabilize. I'll also bump the autoscaler target and temporarily add +2 pods to the pool. @samir can you confirm there are available GPUs in the spare pool to add?

samir: I see spare capacity in dedicated-pool-3. I can trigger a temporary allocation to scale up by 2 nodes. Doing it now. Also will check if there was a bad quantization kernel pushed in the last deploy.

[sre-bot]: ACTION: scaling dedicated-pool-3 by +2 nodes (requested by samir). Change propagated to cluster manager. Link: https://infra.example/change/cc-992

maria: drafted a customer update, please review before I post to Zendesk: 
> Hi AcmePayments — we’ve identified a transient resource pressure in the serving pool that caused model load churn and upstream 502/503s. We’ve bumped capacity and routed your traffic to a lower-memory model variant while we investigate. You should see errors drop; we’ll follow up with a full postmortem and ETA to restore your default model. If you need immediate rollback to previous behavior, let us know and we can pin your traffic. — Maria

leah: good. Add an apology line and include the repro request id and a short mitigation timeline. Also cc SRE SLA folks. Suggest: "We increased capacity at 09:30 UTC and performed a model routing change at 09:34 UTC; error rate reduced from ~18% to <1% within ~8 minutes."

josh: quick note about SDKs: customer reported their SDK retry loop was making it worse because default retries were immediate. Recommend they use exponential backoff and max_retries=4. Sample python snippet to share:```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=KEY, timeout=90, retries={"max_attempts":4, "backoff":"exponential", "base":0.5})
resp = client.generate("redwood-2.1", "...", stream=False)
```

maria: posted the update to Zendesk with the timeline + request ids. Customer replied: "Thanks — we see much fewer errors now, will continue testing." :thumbsup:

samir: root cause hypothesis for initial triage: concurrent model loads + memory pressure on runtime nodes caused evictions; that triggered upstream 502s as in-flight requests lost their worker. Follow-ups: (1) investigate why autoscaler didn't pre-warm nodes for load pattern, (2) verify quantization kernel rollouts (any deploy last night?), (3) add circuit-breaker metrics to avoid immediate 5xx propagation to customers.

josh: confirmed post-mitigation metrics: 5xx rate in prod-west-1 dropped to 0.7% by 09:42 UTC, error budget safe. Rolling restarts finished. I'll create incident for postmortem and link to actions: https://incidents.example/P-2026-03-15-87

leah: thanks team. Next actions: samir to verify deploys/kernels and provide postmortem draft, josh to add recommended autoscaler tuning, maria to follow up with customer in 24h. I'll coordinate the postmortem and SLA impacts.

maria: closing the immediate escalation. Customer confirm message at 09:46: "we're good — thanks for the fast response". Will keep thread open until we have the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
